executive_assessment.text: The project ESMF describes northwest urban clusters 1 and 2 as relatively drought-prone, with less rainfall and higher temperatures than other parts of Bangladesh.
The note reports that climate change, pollution, resource overuse, and rapid urbanization are degrading ecosystems and increasing livelihood threats, especially for the rural poor.
RUTDP plans climate-resilient urban services and stronger city management across 87 municipalities and city corporations in 36 districts, targeting about 21 million people, half of them women.

geographic_notes.text: Northwest urban clusters 1 and 2: The project ESMF describes northwest urban clusters 1 and 2 as relatively drought-prone, with less rainfall and higher temperatures than other parts of Bangladesh.
Southwest urban clusters 3 and 5; coastal districts: Coastal districts in southwest clusters 3 and 5 are described as vulnerable to salinity intrusion, cyclones, and tidal water surges.

87 selected municipalities and city corporations; 36 districts in five divisions: RUTDP plans climate-resilient urban services and stronger city management across 87 municipalities and city corporations in 36 districts, targeting about 21 million people, half of them women.

low-lying coastal delta; coastal areas: The note describes low-lying delta populations as exposed to cyclones and storm surges, with coastal erosion and seawater intrusion affecting land and groundwater.

Bangladesh coastal villages: Studies cited by the note estimate mangroves protect 1.1-3.5 million people from cyclone flooding; villages with mangroves had about half the monetary losses of other villages during Cyclone Sidr.

Bangladesh; 64 districts; six Delta Plan ecological zones: The paper says Bangladesh's Delta Plan 2100 divides 64 districts into six ecological zones and identifies 58 districts as extremely vulnerable to climate change.

Barind and drought-prone areas; coastal regions: The paper reports regional health differences: groundwater depletion in Barind and drought-prone areas, saline drinking water on the coast, and especially pronounced effects for pregnant women and children.
